Thanks Elena — quick clarifications before we ask for an updated quote: 

On hybrid specifics:
- Expected onsite + staff: 48 attendees (plus 6 staff).
- Expected remote attendees: ~12; remote speakers: up to 3 who will present slides and take Q&A.
- We will use Microsoft Teams as the default meeting platform for our execs, but we are open to using an RTMP stream to a private CDN if that gives better reliability. Can you confirm if you can output both (Teams + RTMP) simultaneously, or whether we need a vendor to run a Teams gateway/bridge?

A/V requirements: 
- Presenter mics: 2 lavs (one spare), 1 handheld for Q&A, and a tabletop ambient mic for roundtable.
- Camera setup: at least two cameras (wide + close-up); PTZ preferred so the tech can frame speakers.
- Recording: full session recording, retained by us for 90 days.
- Breakouts: each breakout needs separate house audio and the option to stream a breakout to a remote-only breakout room if required.

Network and redundancy: 
- We request a redundant internet path (secondary 500Mbps) for the event day and the option for a static IP or VPN termination for Redwood to access internal resources.

Logistics: 
- We need a 90-minute window on the morning of Dec 8 for full setup and a dry run with at least one remote speaker.
- Hotel room block: Samir from our travel team will coordinate attendee stays; I cc'd him on the next thread.

Can Aaron or your AV contact propose a revised line-item quote that separates out redundancy (encoders, backup uplink), Teams gateway/bridge, and day-of tech staffing? If you can include a suggested run-of-show and an outline for a hybrid rehearsal, that would be great.

Thanks for the detail. I’m Aaron from AVWorks; I’ve attached a revised AV quote (AV_quote_v3.pdf) that splits out the items you asked for. Highlights and quick technical notes: 

- Dual-stream approach: We can run a Teams meeting in the room (using a Teams Rooms bridge) and simultaneously push an RTMP feed to a private CDN for remote stakeholders. This requires an encoder that can duplicate the stream; I’ve itemized the encoder rental and licensing.
- Cameras: Recommended setup is 2x PTZ (one wide, one close) + 1 static wide for audience shots. PTZ control is via IP over VLAN.
- Redundancy: Recommend a redundant uplink (primary 1Gbps + secondary 500Mbps bonded) with an on-site bonded cellular fallback (3x 5G gateways) for failover.
- Audio: 2 lav + 1 handheld + one ambient table mic; wired console with DI boxes for presenter laptops.
- Breakouts: Oak A/B/C can be fitted with discrete audio and a single AV rack per room; streaming individual breakouts will require per-room encoders (quoted).
- On-site crew: lead tech (8 hours), camera operator (8 hours) for PTZs, and a streaming engineer (6 hours) for the Teams/RTMP bridge and recording.

Network requirements (for IT to provision):
- Dedicated VLANs for AV gear with QoS; one static public IP for encoder traffic or a VPN tunnel termination point.
- Minimum reserved bandwidth during event: 1.5Gbps aggregate for the venue if streaming multiple rooms concurrently.

We can schedule a 60–90 minute technical dry run on the morning of Dec 8 (preferred) or the day before if you can provide remote speaker availability. Please confirm whether Redwood will manage the Teams meeting instance or if AVWorks should host/manage the Teams Rooms booking.

I attached AV_quote_v3.pdf with line items and optional add-ons. Let me know if you want me to include a diagram for camera placement and encoder rack layout — I can sketch that and drop into the Drive link.

Cheers,
